Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 8.24. Exact Sanskrit: अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् ।
तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥ २४ ॥ Exact stored meaning: Fire, light, daytime, the bright fortnight (śukla-pakṣa), and the six months of the northern solstice (uttarāyaṇa) — departing in these, the knowers of Brahman (brahma-vidaḥ) go to Brahman. Chapter context: The imperishable, remembrance, transition, cosmic cycles and paths. Use symbolic contemplative imagery without depicting bodily distress, corpses or literal metaphysical claims as historical events. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: O best of the Bharatas, I will describe the times (paths) in which yogīs departing attain non-return (anāvṛttim — liberation) and return (āvṛttim — rebirth). Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Smoke, night, the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇa-pakṣa), and the six months of the southern solstice (dakṣiṇāyana) — in these, the yogī reaches the lunar light (cāndramasaṃ jyotir) and returns. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
